strengths: Yes: the worldbuilding is done through mechanism and use. The Quieting arrives at a marked stride; survey history lives in scaled and bent iron; road lore belongs to Oryn's patients; research happens through timed stones, page custody, and cold tests; the animal's rule becomes something the unit can act on rather than a dossier paragraph.

Yes: the fight is memorably choreographed at the design level, and terrain is load-bearing far beyond the two-beat minimum. The causeway enforces approach, standing weight triggers the first strike, the coping is refuge and fall hazard, shallow water enables skipping movement, and the broken center becomes the fixed-point trap. The win is writable as: Cael removed the wyrm's ability to choose its target by giving the flooded floor one point that never moved.

The teaching sequence is strong fairness work. Two different stone behaviors isolate settled weight from sound, then the Anchor trial proves the exact interaction the climax needs. Karis's and Cael's fixed lines distinguish their mental models without changing the shared finding.

Oryn remains a healer in action rather than being converted into a fighter. She enters because a patient is falling, chooses the shortest route, applies the tested movement rule, and later pays the reserve cost outside the line. The final 'So are you' lands because the practical route has been her relationship vocabulary all book.

The found-family labor stays differentiated under pressure: Brom supplies weight and wall knowledge; Seln converts observation into a rule; Karis copies because the evidence is the objective; Lira adapts one-armed; Cael turns the rule; Oryn reaches the patient. Preserve this division of competence during repair.

The chapter protects the packet's restraint: the wyrm is not killed or read, the tenth fragment stays unused, no mind or Path is assigned, hidden Quieting theory remains withheld, and the ending trusts dialogue after Chapter 20's log.

draft_evidence.quote: They spent the afternoon outside the line on trials, and he wrote it as one, because Karis would, and because the six of them had walked into two floors on folklore and a stake and had learned twice what that cost.

comparison_evidence.quote: He did it from the wall's top, with Karis on the coping beside him timing it by her own count, because she did not trust a count she had not made.

findings.consequence: The hall wall is at the center of a two-hundred-meter Quieting perimeter, so Cael and Karis cannot remain outside the line while standing on its coping. Brom and Lira also use the coping during the stone trials, yet the chapter later says the party first goes in at dawn. The manuscript therefore skips an entry and contradicts its own risk boundary. The packet itself requires both OUTSIDE-the-line teaching and the wall-top Anchor trial, so a compliant repair needs an authority ruling on which spatial requirement governs.
findings.repair_target: Resolve the packet's outside-line versus wall-top conflict explicitly, then stage every trial and boundary crossing at physically compatible locations without silently changing the two-hundred-meter perimeter or the required cold test.

draft_evidence.quote: "Something's been up the bank," Seln said. "Something big enough to leave that, and it went back into the water, and it lives in the water, and the water's inside the line." He did not stand up. "I don't like the stake."

comparison_evidence.quote: "It can't see," Seln said, along the coping. "It can't leave the water. It can't reach a coping. As long as nobody's on the floor, it's a thing in a pond."

findings.consequence: The draft first identifies a large water-dwelling creature as having traveled up the bank and returned to the water, then makes the opposite rule load-bearing in the fight. The packet permits only a water-bound wyrm and requires approval for any behavior beyond that set, so readers cannot know whether the coping is actually safe.
findings.repair_target: Keep the churned ground without attributing out-of-water travel to the wyrm, and preserve a single consistent, evidence-supported water-bound rule before the wall refuge depends on it.

draft_evidence.quote: Brom put his weight where he was told. He was on his feet in the shallows with Oryn's hands in his coat and the shoulder pouring, and he went to the wall's foot beside the broken centre, where the wall's inner face came down into the water two strides from the thing's pale side, and put his back to the stone and his good shoulder into the wall and his whole weight *down*, so that for the length of the strike there were two things on the floor that stayed — a fixed point and a big man — and the thing under the spring had its jaws on one and its flank to the other and could not turn.

comparison_evidence.quote: Six people on a coping a boot wide, a shoulder's height above a flooded floor, in a square forty strides on a side, and the thing under the floor going round the inside of it under the water. He catalogued the terrain because the terrain was the fight: the coping was cover, because nothing on the floor could reach a shoulder's height; the coping was a trap, because it was a boot wide and stone and wet, and a foot that went off it went into a boot of water with the rule waiting; the water was a boot deep everywhere and then, at the middle, where the floor had broken and the spring came up, deep — deep enough that the length of the thing could turn in it, which it did, and which was where it went to turn. And it could not leave the water. He had watched the churned mud at the line and the bent stake at the lip and had the whole of what the roads knew, and the whole of it was *comes up*; nothing said *comes out*. It was a thing of the floor and the water on the floor, and the walls were not floor.

findings.consequence: A central breach in a forty-stride square is roughly twenty strides from a perimeter wall, but the climax places that wall two strides from the wyrm's pale side and both coping shooters four meters away. The invented forty-stride dimension makes the packet's contact-range team strike physically unreconstructable at the pivotal beat.
findings.repair_target: Reconcile the hall dimensions, broken-center position, wyrm length, Brom's wall brace, and both shooters' contact range so the same map governs the whole fight.

draft_evidence.quote: From the coping. Seln with his own bow, kneeling, at four meters, two bolts into the pale in the time it took the jaws to close twice. Lira with Oryn's — the crossbow she did not know how to wind and had learned in a week to brace one-armed against the coping and her knee and fire, badly, and at four meters into a thing the size of a cart badly was enough — two bolts, one into the pale and one into the water beside it, which was, at that range, one-armed, the best shot anyone had made in the hall.

comparison_evidence.quote: Seln and Lira (one-armed, a crossbow braced) put two bolts each into the pale underside the strike exposes, at contact range.

findings.consequence: The packet requires four underside hits, but Lira's second bolt misses; the next paragraph nevertheless counts four bolts in the pale. The same sentence gives her two rapid shots from a crossbow she cannot wind, and the closing scene later puts a bolt in that crossbow without staging any reload. The decisive exchange therefore fails both its fixed outcome and basic equipment causality.
findings.repair_target: Stage a physically legible one-armed firing and reload solution, deliver two underside hits from each assigned shooter, and keep the later weapon state consistent with the bolts actually fired.

draft_evidence.quote: She had gone over the stone first, with Brom's coat in her fist, and had stopped, and checked her hands, and said "Back," and had not said anything else, because Brom was on his knees on the track with his shoulder open front and back along the mark she had made three days before, and she had both hands on it before he had finished kneeling. An hour. Karis timed it. It was the second time she had mended that shoulder, and she said so, once, to the shoulder — "Twice. It'll hold twice. It will not hold three times this season, so don't ask it to." — and Brom said, "Arm," and she said, "No," and he didn't.

comparison_evidence.quote:
*Hundred and fifteenth day. The Long Stair, the rim, at the stone. A hundred and eight in hand; nothing owed; three hundred entered as taken and never to be paid. Nineteen. Ten. Brom's shoulder mended and not used. Lira's arm closed and not used. Seln's got a ledger. Karis has twenty-nine sheets and a number, and the number is forty-one.*

*Instruments recovered. The contract's paid, and the man who posted it is never going to see them, because Seln's keeping the ledger and I'm keeping the kit. Someone measured this place five years ago and wrote bearing and stopped. Karis has a straightedge. She's been waiting her whole life to use it. The Ring, the Stair, and whatever's on that bearing. Pike said a handful. We have two. The kit says three. We're going to go look.*

findings.consequence: Oryn makes the first shoulder mark before Chapter 20; Chapter 20 then occupies the next day, Chapter 21 travels for three days, and the fight occurs after another overnight. 'Three days before' cannot reconcile with that sequence and corrupts the injury ledger the chapter otherwise carefully carries.
findings.repair_target: Correct the elapsed-time reference to match the Chapter 19 mend, Chapter 20's dated day, the three-day journey, and the dawn fight without changing the required second-mending count.

draft_evidence.quote: Not on the track. On the marsh's dry edge, back to the stone, boots in the reeds, wet to the waist, hands in her lap, face grey, eyes on the hall, and she did not say anything for a long while, and nobody asked her to, because the unit had learned at three lines what a healer looked like when she had spent the whole of a route's budget on two people in a morning, and it looked like this.

comparison_evidence.quote:
The costs, outside the line, on the track's dry end, with Oryn's hands back at the stride.

She had gone over the stone first, with Brom's coat in her fist, and had stopped, and checked her hands, and said "Back," and had not said anything else, because Brom was on his knees on the track with his shoulder open front and back along the mark she had made three days before, and she had both hands on it before he had finished kneeling. An hour. Karis timed it. It was the second time she had mended that shoulder, and she said so, once, to the shoulder — "Twice. It'll hold twice. It will not hold three times this season, so don't ask it to." — and Brom said, "Arm," and she said, "No," and he didn't.

Then she sat down.

findings.consequence: Only Brom receives a mending in this morning's staged aftermath; Oryn does not heal or read Cael before sitting down. The claim that two people consumed the route budget invents a second treatment and weakens the otherwise explicit causal accounting for her depletion.
findings.repair_target: Make the stated reserve expenditure match the single staged mending, or stage and authorize any additional treatment before counting it; preserve Oryn's required drained silence.

draft_evidence.quote: He saw it turn because he had the Iron read on the floor under the water and the floor told him where a thing the weight of a cart was pushing on it: the length going past her under the water and coming round, not to where she had been, but to where she was *going*, because she was going to Brom, and Brom had stopped, and Brom was the heaviest thing on the floor, and a healer who reached a stopped man was going to stop.

comparison_evidence.quote: **6.2 — Every rule visibly costs.** Magic, rank, and institutional privilege all price in: access, fatigue, money, standing, time. Check: any use of Path ability in a scene must name or show its cost at least once per chapter per ability

findings.consequence: The Iron read is active more than once and supplies crucial floor geography and warning of the second pass, but the chapter's cost ledger bills only Compression and Anchor. That makes a tactically decisive third fragment read as selectively free inside a scene built around visible receipts.
findings.repair_target: Name or show the Iron read's established per-chapter cost or attention constraint while preserving the fragment inventory and the two primary winning components.
